the development of a monocular SLAM system that can robustly reconstruct dynamic objects in a real-time setting.
the problem of estimating the pose and shape of dynamic objects, using a single moving monocular camera.
the development of a novel real-time system that can localize dynamic objects in a monocular video stream, using only prior knowledge of the category of the object.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel shape-prior model for monocular object localization that can be used to estimate the 3D shape and pose of objects from a single moving camera.

we present a system for monocular localization of dynamic objects in the context of a moving camera, that is able to perform real-time 3D shape recovery, while accounting for self-occlusion and 2D localization error.
we present a real time system for monocular object localization and reconstruction, that is robust to dynamic environments and occlusions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by incorporating shape priors, we can obtain detailed object reconstructions, even in the presence of severe 2D localization and tracking errors.
, by incorporating shape priors, we can obtain accurate 3D shape and pose estimates for dynamic objects in real-world scenarios, using a single moving monocular camera and no prior 3D information.
, even though the problem of object pose estimation in dynamic environments is ill-posed, the incorporation of shape priors can be leveraged to obtain accurate and robust pose and shape estimates.
